To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the fetal liver is an excellent source of erythropoietic cells; and 2) the fetal liver and umbi­c­al cord blood are both excellent sources of erythroid progenitor cells that can be grown in culture.
erythroid colony formation was studied in plasma clot cultures containing cells from human fetal liver (FL), umbilical cord (CB) and adult peripheral blood (APB).
fetal liver and umblicial cord blood cells produce large numbers of erythroid colonies in vitro, and that the cells in these colonies produce β and γ globins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the erythroid progenitor cells of human fetal liver, cord blood and adult bone marrow.
the development of in vitro systems to study human haemopoietic stem cells.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of erythroid cell differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are not conclusive and that more studies are needed.
erythropoiesis is an orderly process in which the stem cell gives rise to the erythroblast and the latter gives rise to the normoblast.
fetal liver and cord blood cells have a greater proliferative capacity than do adult bone marrow cells and that this is associated with an increased capacity for erythropoietic differentiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
erythroid colonies from fetal liver, umbili‐cal cord blood and peripheral blood are similar in morphology and in their response to Epo and differ in their kinetics of colony appearance.

erythroid progenitor cells in fetal liver are more numerous and more easily cultured than in adult bone marrow or adult peripheral blood, and the former are also more easily stimulated to colony formation than the latter.
erythroid progenitors from FL and CB are more numerous and more responsive to Epo than are the same progenitors from adult PB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can use the umbilical cord to create stem cells.
the use of human umbilical cord and placental blood as a source for hematopoietic stem cell transplantation is safe and effective in the treatment of patients with hematopoietic disorders.

the use of human fetal liver and umblicord blood cells for erythroid culture is a very promising approach for the development of in vitro culture methods that can be used in the study of the erythroid differentiation process.
